# Reliance Industries Limited – Research Brief (as of June 10, 2026)

**Symbol:** RELIANCE (NSE)  
**Sector:** Energy | **Industry:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing [39]

## Overview
Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is India’s largest company by market capitalisation (~₹17.03 trn) [39]. Its businesses span oil-to-chemicals (O2C), telecom (Jio), retail, and increasingly, digital infrastructure. The latest audited results were approved on April 24, 2026 [1].

## Recent Financial Performance
- **Q4 FY2026 & Full-Year:** The board approved results on April 24, 2026 [1]. Overall EBITDA was flat; O2C segment EBITDA declined 4% QoQ, while consumer businesses (Jio + Retail) combined EBITDA grew 14% QoQ [1]. **No standalone/consolidated revenue, net profit, or segment-level figures for Q4 or FY2026 are available in the provided filings.**
- **Trailing Twelve Months (as of June 10, 2026):** Revenue ~₹10.57 trn, net income ~₹808 bn, profit margin ~7.6% (yfinance aggregate) [36].

## Strategic Developments
- On **June 10, 2026**, Reliance announced a partnership with Meta to develop an AI-enabled data centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat [5]. This reinforces RIL’s push into AI infrastructure and long-term digital investments.

| ROE | 9.14% | [39] |

## Outlook
- The divergence between flat O2C EBITDA and strong consumer segment growth (Jio + Retail up 14% QoQ) persists [1]. The Q4 analyst call provided no forward guidance on capex, deleveraging, or FY2027 projections [1].
- The AI‑infrastructure partnership with Meta signals continued long‑term technology investment, though its near‑term financial impact is not yet quantifiable [5].
- **No FY2027 revenue, profit, or debt‑target projections are available in this run.**
